blueprint_concepts: Concept of image in three dimensional geometry
Foot of perpendicular and image of a point in a line
english: Let $L$ be the line $\dfrac{x}{2}=y-2=\dfrac{z-5}{2}$ and let $A$ be the point $(-3,-1,5)$. Let $\Pi$ be the plane $x+2y+\lambda z=k$, where $\lambda$ and $k$ are real numbers, such that the image of $A$ in $\Pi$ coincides with the image of $A$ in the line $L$. Then the value of $\lambda+k$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $L$ रेखा $\dfrac{x}{2}=y-2=\dfrac{z-5}{2}$ है तथा $A$ बिन्दु $(-3,-1,5)$ है। माना कि $\Pi$ तल $x+2y+\lambda z=k$ है, जहाँ $\lambda$ तथा $k$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं, इस प्रकार कि तल $\Pi$ में $A$ का प्रतिबिम्ब, रेखा $L$ में $A$ के प्रतिबिम्ब के सम्पाती है। तब $\lambda+k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The image of $A$ in $\Pi$ is $B$ only if $\Pi$ is the perpendicular bisector plane of $AB$: normal $\parallel\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,4,-4)\parallel(1,2,-2)\Rightarrow\lambda=-2$
solution_full: A general point of $L$ is $(2t,\ 2+t,\ 5+2t)$ and the direction of $L$ is $(2,1,2)$.
For the foot $N$ of the perpendicular from $A(-3,-1,5)$: $\overrightarrow{AN}=(2t+3,\ t+3,\ 2t)$ and $\overrightarrow{AN}\cdot(2,1,2)=2(2t+3)+(t+3)+2(2t)=9t+9=0$, so $t=-1$ and $N=(-2,1,3)$.
The image of $A$ in $L$ is $B$ with $N$ the midpoint of $AB$: $B=2N-A=(-4+3,\ 2+1,\ 6-5)=(-1,3,1)$.

The image of $A$ in a plane is $B$ exactly when the plane is perpendicular to $AB$ and passes through the midpoint of $AB$. Here $\overrightarrow{AB}=(2,4,-4)=2(1,2,-2)$ and the midpoint is $N(-2,1,3)$.
The normal $(1,2,\lambda)$ of $\Pi$ must be parallel to $(1,2,-2)$, so $\lambda=-2$.
originality_note: New: a plane is fixed by requiring that it reflects a point to the same place as a given line does, so the plane is the perpendicular bisector of the point and its line image (way 5). Closest known: image of a point in a line; image of a point in a plane. Different because: the two image concepts are tied by an equality that determines two unknown coefficients of the plane.

concept_use.Concept of image in three dimensional ge: Image of A in the plane Pi equals B exactly when Pi is the perpendicular bisector plane of AB, giving lambda and k.
concept_use.Foot of perpendicular and image of a poi: Foot of the perpendicular N from A to the line L and the image B = 2N - A.

key_step: Foot of perpendicular on the line, then reading the plane as the perpendicular bisector of A and its image.
justification: Routine chain of two standard image constructions and one comparison of coefficients, no insight. Between the one-step plane question 2024-P2-Q6 (L1) and the foot-of-perpendicular chain 2026-P2-Q7 (L3).
